title: Dependency manifest or lock file served from the web root
summary: The site serves its composer, npm, yarn, Ruby or Python lock file to anybody. It lists every library and its exact version, which tells an attacker which known vulnerabilities to try first, and it shows that the project folder itself is the web root, so other files beside it may be served too.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist, so a site that answers every path with the same page is not mistaken for one serving the file.
confirm.differential: status_in(200) and body_differs(control) and body_matches("(?m)\"content-hash\"\\s*:\\s*\"[0-9a-f]{32}\"|\"lockfileVersion\"\\s*:\\s*\\d|^# yarn lockfile v1|^GEM\\s*$\\s+remote:|\"_meta\"\\s*:\\s*\\{\\s*\"hash\"|^# This file is automatically @generated by Poetry|\"require\"\\s*:\\s*\\{[^}]*\"php\"\\s*:")

reproduce: curl -sk 'https://host/composer.lock' | head -20 and look for "content-hash" and a "packages" list. Try package-lock.json ("lockfileVersion"), yarn.lock ("# yarn lockfile v1"), Gemfile.lock ("GEM" then "remote:"), Pipfile.lock ("_meta") and poetry.lock. Compare with a path that cannot exist, so a page served for every path is not mistaken for the file.
remediate: Serve the application from a public folder that holds only what browsers need, not from the project root. If that cannot change yet, deny dependency and lock files in the web server (for Apache: <FilesMatch "^(composer\.(json|lock)|package(-lock)?\.json|yarn\.lock|Gemfile\.lock|Pipfile\.lock|poetry\.lock)$"> Require all denied </FilesMatch>).
